title: Bochner Generalization of intervalIntegral_swap: Banach-Valued Fubini for Interval Integrals
description: S3 ACT: closes the S2 sorries, delivering all three intervalIntegral_swap theorems for a Banach codomain E (NormedAddCommGroup + NormedSpace ℝ + CompleteSpace) with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. (1) Ordered case `intervalIntegral_swap_of_le` (proved S2) reduces to `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap` after Icc → Ioc restriction via `Measure.prod_mono`. (2) General case `intervalIntegral_swap` (proved S3) handles four sign sub-cases of (a ≤ b vs a > b) × (c ≤ d vs c > d) via sign-flip helpers `flip_bounds_E` and `neg_outside_E`; the parent's four `linarith` calls are replaced by `rw + neg_neg` (the underlying identity is additive-abelian, not order-theoretic). (3) Continuous case `intervalIntegral_swap_of_continuous` (proved S3) reduces to the general case using `Continuous.measurable` and `ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact`. Confirms the S1 OBSERVE finding that the parent's real-valued proof is fully codomain-generic.

meta.historicalContext: Fubini's theorem (Fubini 1907) states that under integrability, ∫∫f dxdy = ∫∫f dydx for any iterated integral. Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap` provides this for the Bochner integral of a function `f : α × β → E` valued in a Banach space E. However, Mathlib does NOT provide a corresponding `intervalIntegral_swap` lemma for the *interval integral* `∫ x in a..b, f x` notation — every application of Fubini to interval integrals must reimplement the Icc/Ioc bridge. The parent slug `greens-theorem-oq-01-oq-01-oq-02` proves three real-valued versions of this missing lemma (ordered case, general case via sign-flip, continuous specialization). This OQ-03 sibling asks the natural follow-up: does the same proof structure work for a Banach codomain E? The S1 OBSERVE audit confirms YES, with no mathematical novelty — the question is purely a portability/codomain-genericity check. This S2 SCAFFOLD ships the first fully-ported lemma (ordered case) and stubs the remaining two for S3.

The continuous case reduces to the general case via `hf.measurable` + `hf.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact` applied to the compact rectangle `uIcc a b ×ˢ uIcc c d`, with `restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict measurableSet_uIcc measurableSet_uIcc` bridging the integrability hypothesis form. overview.historicalContext: Fubini's theorem (Fubini 1907; Tonelli 1909) is foundational for multi-dimensional integration. The Bochner integral (Bochner 1933) extends Lebesgue integration to Banach-valued functions, and the corresponding Bochner Fubini theorem appears in modern functional-analytic measure theory (Diestel-Uhl 1977 *Vector Measures*, Mathlib4 `MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod`). The interval-integral notation `∫ x in a..b, f x` is standard for one-variable real analysis and is set up in Mathlib4 to be syntactically convenient even when `a > b` (in which case the integral is interpreted as the negative of the reverse integral, via `integral_symm`). The codomain genericity of the interval-integral construction follows from the codomain genericity of the underlying `MeasureTheory.integral`, which Mathlib4 has had for Banach-valued functions since its early versions. Thus the Bochner generalization of `intervalIntegral_swap` is mathematically routine: every lemma involved is already stated for Banach codomains. The interest of this gallery entry is purely as a worked-out *verification* of the codomain genericity claim and as a building block for downstream Bochner-valued vector-calculus formalizations (Green's theorem, Stokes' theorem, divergence theorem for Banach-valued differential forms).
overview.problemStatement: Does `intervalIntegral_swap` (Fubini for one-variable interval integrals) generalize from real-valued to Banach-valued integrands? Answer: yes, verbatim, with `linarith → rw + neg_neg` substitution in the sign analysis (the underlying identity is additive-abelian, not order-theoretic).
overview.proofStrategy: Verbatim port from the parent file's real-valued proofs, parametrized over `E : NormedAddCommGroup, NormedSpace ℝ E, CompleteSpace E`. The ordered case is mechanical: rewrite both `∫ x in a..b, f x` as `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂volume` via `integral_of_le`, upgrade integrability from Icc-product to Ioc-product via `Measure.prod_mono`, then close with `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap`. The general case threads sign-flip identities (`flip_bounds_E`, `neg_outside_E`) through a four-way case split on `(a ≤ b vs a > b) × (c ≤ d vs c > d)`; the parent's four `linarith` calls become `rw [..., neg_neg]` (or `simp only [neg_neg]` for the four-flip Case 4). The continuous case reduces to the general case via `Continuous.measurable` + `ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact` on the compact rectangle `uIcc a b ×ˢ uIcc c d`, with `restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict measurableSet_uIcc measurableSet_uIcc` bridging the integrability hypothesis. All three theorems are codomain-generic with no Mathlib gaps.
keyInsights: **Codomain genericity is `free` for interval-integral Fubini**: Every Mathlib lemma the parent invokes is already stated for Bochner integrands. The S1 OBSERVE audit catalogued every dependency and confirmed no real-valuedness is exploited.

**linarith → abel is the only manual substitution**: The parent's general-case proof has four `linarith` invocations in the sign analysis of the four (a≤b vs a>b) × (c≤d vs c>d) sub-cases. Each `linarith` closes a step of the form `α + β = -(-α - β)` in ℝ; the same identity holds in any additive-abelian group, where `abel` directly closes it.

**Ordered case is the smallest buildable witness**: The S2 deliverable is the *ordered case* fully proven for E. This is the smallest fragment that demonstrates codomain genericity end-to-end (the proof uses every key Bochner-generic lemma except the sign flip). The general case and continuous case are stubs.

**No measurability subtlety in the Bochner setting**: For Banach E, the predicate `Measurable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => f p.1 p.2)` uses the *Borel* σ-algebra on E (assumed via `NormedAddCommGroup` + `MeasurableSpace` instance). Mathlib automatically supplies this; no `MeasurableSpace.borel` workaround needed.

**Integrability hypothesis is on the product restriction measure**: The hypothesis `Integrable (fun p => f p.1 p.2) ((volume.restrict (Icc a b)).prod (volume.restrict (Icc c d)))` is preserved from the parent, with the product-measure monotonicity argument deriving Ioc-restriction integrability via `Measure.prod_mono` and `Measure.restrict_mono Ioc_subset_Icc_self`. This step is codomain-agnostic.

sections.title: Setup and Codomain Variables
sections.summary: Imports MeasureTheory.IntervalIntegral, MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod, MeasureTheory.Measure.Prod, and Mathlib.Tactic. Documents the S1 OBSERVE audit confirming codomain genericity. Opens the namespace and introduces the variable block `{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]`.
sections.mathContext: Setup: Banach codomain $E$ with $\mathrm{NormedSpace}\ \mathbb{R}\ E$ and $\mathrm{CompleteSpace}\ E$. The Bochner integral is defined for any such $E$ in Mathlib4.

sections.title: Ordered Case (fully proved)
sections.summary: Proves `intervalIntegral_swap_of_le` for `f : ℝ → ℝ → E` by verbatim port of the parent's real-valued script. The proof rewrites both iterated interval integrals to ordinary Bochner integrals on `Ioc`, then applies `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap` after restricting via `Measure.prod_mono` and `Measure.restrict_mono Ioc_subset_Icc_self`.
sections.mathContext: If $f: \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \to E$ is measurable and integrable on $[a,b] \times [c,d]$ with $a \le b, c \le d$, then $\int_c^d \int_a^b f(x,y)\,dx\,dy = \int_a^b \int_c^d f(x,y)\,dy\,dx$.

sections.title: Sign-Flip Helpers (Bochner-valued, fully proved)
sections.summary: Private theorems `flip_bounds_E` (`∫ x in a..b, f x = -∫ x in b..a, f x`) and `neg_outside_E` (`∫ x in a..b, -g x = -∫ x in a..b, g x`) for Bochner integrals. Both are one-line ports of the parent's real-valued helpers.
sections.mathContext: Sign-flip: $\int_a^b f\,dx = -\int_b^a f\,dx$ (interval-integral convention). Negation extraction: $\int_a^b (-g)\,dx = -\int_a^b g\,dx$.

sections.title: General Case (S3 proven)
sections.summary: Proves `intervalIntegral_swap` for `f : ℝ → ℝ → E` with no ordering hypothesis on `(a,b)` or `(c,d)`, requiring only measurability + integrability on the `uIcc` product. Splits on the four sign possibilities of `(a ≤ b vs a > b)` × `(c ≤ d vs c > d)`. Cases 2/3 thread three sign-flip equalities through `rw [..., neg_neg]`; Case 4 (both reversed) threads five sign-flip equalities with `simp only [neg_neg]` closing the quadruple negation. The parent's four `linarith` calls are replaced by these explicit rewrites — the underlying identity is additive-abelian, not order-theoretic.
sections.mathContext: General Fubini: $\int_c^d \int_a^b f\,dx\,dy = \int_a^b \int_c^d f\,dy\,dx$ for arbitrary $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$, under integrability on the unordered product rectangle.

sections.title: Continuous Case (S3 proven)
sections.summary: Proves `intervalIntegral_swap_of_continuous` for `f : ℝ → ℝ → E` with no measurability or integrability hypotheses. Extracts measurability via `hf.measurable` and integrability via `hf.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact` on the compact rectangle `uIcc a b ×ˢ uIcc c d`, bridging the hypothesis form via `restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict measurableSet_uIcc measurableSet_uIcc`.
sections.mathContext: Continuous Fubini: for $f: \mathbb{R}^2 \to E$ continuous, the iterated interval integrals on any $(a,b) \times (c,d)$ rectangle coincide automatically.

conclusion.summary: This S2 SCAFFOLD ports the parent's first `intervalIntegral_swap` theorem (ordered case) to a Banach codomain `E` (NormedAddCommGroup, NormedSpace ℝ, CompleteSpace) by *verbatim* reuse of the parent's real-valued proof. The two private sign-flip helpers (`flip_bounds_E`, `neg_outside_E`) are also fully proven for E. The general case and the continuous-function specialization are stated for E with `sorry`, awaiting S3 (a 4-way sign analysis where the parent's four `linarith` calls become `abel`).
conclusion.implications: The Bochner integral is the standard tool for Banach-valued integration in analysis and probability — empirical processes, vector measures, stochastic processes, Banach-valued differential forms. Having a working `intervalIntegral_swap` for Banach codomains is a building block for any one-dimensional vector-calculus development (Green's theorem, Stokes' theorem, divergence theorem) phrased over Mathlib's `∫ x in a..b, f x` notation rather than the lower-level `∫ x in s, f x ∂μ`. More broadly, the audit-then-port workflow demonstrated here is a template for handling Mathlib codomain-generalization questions efficiently: catalog the dependencies, identify the *only* tactic that is codomain-specific (`linarith`), and substitute (`abel`). This pattern keeps the gallery's Banach-valued extensions in lockstep with their real-valued parents without duplicating mathematical effort.
openQuestions: Does the same audit-then-port pattern work for the *signed* measure setting (replacing `volume` with a general signed measure of bounded variation)? The Mathlib API around `Measure.prod` is structured for `MeasureTheory.Measure` (positive), so signed-measure Fubini would need an additional Jordan-decomposition step.

Can `intervalIntegral_swap` be extended to a *locally convex* codomain (not necessarily normed), using Pettis integration in place of Bochner? Mathlib does not currently have a developed Pettis-integral API, so this would require infrastructure work.

What is the cleanest way to phrase the Banach-valued analogue of Green's theorem (∮ closed-curve integral = ∬ region integral) on top of this Fubini lemma? The natural target is `f : ℝ² → E` with `E` Banach, where the line integral is the standard Riemann-Stieltjes type and the area integral is Bochner.
